page.layout: One printed page (left page of the spread): running head at top with page number 206 at the top left; one column of running text with a heading-like numbered paragraph (XXVII.) and two further paragraphs; catchword at the lower right. No marginal notes on this page. The narrow strip at the right edge belongs to the neighbouring page and is not transcribed.

main_text.l: Reipublicæ salutarem, aut saltem bono publico nihil
incommodaturam, suffragiis suis confirment, ut
ipsis etiam consentientibus abeat in Legem. Qui
fere fuit apud Romanos olim, stante abhuc Repub.
rogandarum Legum mos: unde & Rogandi vox obti-
neat, cujus apud Romanarum rerum scriptores fre-
quentissima mentio est.
XXVII. Ultimus & supremus gradus, (quæ est
ipsissima illa Populi Libertas, quâ tandiu sub op-
timis Regibus ad invidiam usque felices fuimus
Britanni, & nihil stupide ingrati nimium nos in-
dignos præstitissemus tantâ felicitate, adhuc fa-
cillimis[?] esse libuisset) est consensus & expressus inter-
rogationem Legis. Cùm scilicet Legis Formulâ
per-scripta, habità priùs inter ipsos justâ & de rebus
& de verbis deliberatione, Procerum regni & del-
egatorum plebis conjunctis suffragiis comprobata,
Regiæ tandem Majestati, (cui uni competit L-
egum ferendarum summa potestas,) exhibetur, ut
ipsius calculo, si id ipsi commodum visum fue-
rit, confirmata, Legis exinde habeat vigorem,
alias irrita sit penitus, nec pro Lege habeatur.
Quæ Legum sanctissimarum[?] ratio, à Majoribus no-
stris prudentissimè excogitata, & ad nostra usque
secula per tot Regum & annorum series tradu-
cta, omnium superiorum ætatum experientia u-
suque comperta est adeò Reipublicæ salutaris: ut
si de movendis loco suo veteribus terminis non
essent intempestivè fœtis[?] (nequid durius dicam)
capi cœpta ccnsilia[?], floruissent adhuc fortassis, ut
Dei olim beneficio, quæ nunc justissimo ipsius
judicio perierunt, eúntque magis magisque
indies Ecclesiæ, Academiæ, Rex, Populus,
Respublica, Res cujusque privata. Quandoquidem non
posse arbitror humano ingenio facilè excogit-

page.notes: Right-hand neighbouring page: only a narrow cropped edge is visible; not transcribed. A dagger-like mark (†) and a small smudge appear near the foot of the text, below "ad moderandam"; probably ink or a stain, not a printed mark, so omitted. Doubtful readings: "facillimis" (line partly obscured), "Legum sanctissimarum" (word hard to read), "fœtis" (word before the parenthesis), "ccnsilia" (printed as shown; possibly a printing error for "consilia"). "saltem", "secula", "usque" and "alias" written with plain s as the long s is printed. Catchword "licentiam" is the first word of the next page.
